findings.passage: For nearly two decades, Indiana has been a leader in ensuring our elections remain secure by requiring voters to have a valid photo ID when they cast their ballot. In 2025, I co-authored a bill to strengthen Indiana's voter ID law by prohibiting student IDs issued by state colleges or universities from being recognized as an ID to vote, since college IDs are less secure than other forms of identification and standards vary from school to school.
findings.note: From his Senate page 'Sticking up for Common Sense', section 'Maintaining election integrity'. Describes the photo ID requirement and says he co-authored a 2025 bill to stop state college or university student IDs from counting as voting ID. Page has no visible date; year taken from the page title and 2026 content.
subjects: student ID not accepted as voting ID

findings.passage: I also supported laws:Preventing a state agency or a local government unit from sending an absentee ballot application to an individual unless the application was requested by that individual or a member of their family; andProviding county clerks and election offices with more tools to help identify registered voters who may be ineligible, or hold inaccurate records, and helping clerks take steps to update, confirm or repeal voter registrations.
findings.note: Same page. He says he supported laws limiting who may send absentee ballot applications and giving clerks tools to check and update voter rolls. Text copied from the page as the page's list items run together without spaces.

findings.passage: The passage of these and other laws is why Indiana is ranked among the top states in the nation for election integrity.
findings.note: Same page. Closing line of the election integrity section.
